steps.say: Bile duct injuries range from a small cystic stump leak to complete transection. The Strasberg scale grades this spectrum from A to E for planning repair.
steps.tx: **Strasberg** (injury grading scale) grades injury from **A** (ay) cystic stump leak through lateral injury to **E** (ee) transection with loss of **biliary confluence** (duct joining point), and type **E** with excised segment length decides the repair level chosen by the expert surgeon.

steps.say: Strictures near the liver hilum need precise height mapping. The Bismuth-Corlette scale locates the stricture from low to hilar separation.
steps.tx: **Bismuth-Corlette** (stricture height scale) types **I** (one) to **V** (five) locate strictures from distal stump over **2 cm** (two centimetres) to hilar separation, with type **V** adding cystic duct injury, guiding the height of **hepaticojejunostomy** (liver-duct bowel join) for safe reconstruction.

steps.say: Most major injuries are preventable with disciplined technique. Seeing two structures clearly before clipping keeps the common duct safe.
steps.tx: **Critical view of safety** (clear two-structure view) with **2** (two) structures, **Rouviere sulcus** (liver groove landmark) and **intraoperative cholangiogram** (on-table dye X-ray) in unclear anatomy prevents most major injuries during difficult cholecystectomy with inflamed anatomy obscuring planes and routine timeouts before any clip is placed.

vis.alt: Surgical illustration of inflamed gallbladder showing cystic plate, cystic artery, cystic duct and common bile duct in the critical view of safety.
vis.caption: Critical view of safety: cystic plate, two structures and common duct displayed before clipping. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: High strictures need a wide drainage join to stay open. Opening the left duct along the hilar plate creates a broad mouth for sewing bowel.
steps.tx: **Hepp-Couinaud** (left-duct opening move) opens the left hepatic duct along the hilar plate for a wide side-to-side **hepaticojejunostomy** (liver-duct bowel join) with **60 to 70 cm** (sixty to seventy centimetres) **Roux limb** (defunctioned bowel length) to prevent reflux cholangitis for lasting drainage.

vis.alt: Side-by-side illustration of Strasberg type E bile duct transection and end-to-side Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy reconstruction.
vis.caption: Strasberg type E injury repaired by end-to-side Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Timing of repair shapes outcomes after injury. Stable patients go early to experts while sepsis forces drainage first.
steps.tx: **Early repair** (prompt expert fix) within **72 hours** (seventy two hours) by a hepatobiliary surgeon matches delayed repair results, while sepsis and inflammation favour drainage first with **definitive repair** (final reconstruction) at **6 weeks** (six weeks) after infection settles fully under cover.

steps.say: A drain that turns yellow after liver surgery signals a bile leak. Comparing drain bilirubin with blood levels grades its severity.
steps.tx: Postoperative bile leak with **drain bilirubin** (tube bile level) over **3 times** (three times) serum on day **3** (three) is ISGLS grade A when self-limiting and grade B or C when needing **ERCP stenting** (endoscopic tube placement) or reoperation for persistent leaks.

steps.say: Bile duct damage often extends to the neighbouring artery. A scan of the vessels protects any planned reconstruction from ischaemia.
steps.tx: Vascular injury with **right hepatic artery** (liver blood pipe) damage accompanies **30 percent** (thirty percent) of major bile duct injuries and needs CT angiography because **ischaemia** (blood loss injury) threatens any repair attempted with stricture and liver abscess risk afterwards despite stenting.

steps.say: Repair is not the end of follow-up. Yearly liver tests and scans catch late strictures before cirrhosis sets in.
steps.tx: Long-term stricture surveillance with liver function and MRCP detects **secondary biliary cirrhosis** (blocked-duct liver scarring), and **redo hepaticojejunostomy** (repeat liver-duct join) suits failed repairs before transplantation is considered with lifelong clinic review and prompt stricture dilation when needed every year without fail.
